body.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix \(\iota\), and let \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\). Suppose the true pooled model has \(\boldsymbol D_0\in\mathfrak G\) and \(\theta_0\in\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol D_0}\), the normalized allocation obeys \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) with \(\rho_j>0\) for every row and \(n_{Sj}/N_S\to\rho_j\) for \(S\in\{A,B\}\), and the weighting and nondegeneracy conditions hold. As \(\min(N_A,N_B)\to\infty\), the declared lexicographic selector satisfies \(\Pr(\widehat{\boldsymbol D}=\boldsymbol D_0)\to1\), while \(\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}-\boldsymbol\tau)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,V_\tau(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0;\iota))\). Plug-in covariance is consistent and scalar Wald intervals have pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\). The conclusion separately uses certified wrong-graph separation, certified global within-graph uniqueness, certified local nonsingularity, certified positive inference-box clearance, the normalized row allocation, and the deterministic selector. Moreover \(\lVert\Sigma_g\rVert_2\leq\lVert\operatorname{diag}(g)\rVert_2^2\lVert M^+\rVert_2^2\lVert\operatorname{diag}(h)^{-1}\rVert_2^2\lVert\Sigma_h\rVert_2\).
body.justification: The inference layer uses exactly the global, local, interior, selector, and covariance objects certified by the decision layer.
body.gap: Chen--Cao--Bu and Carrasco--Florens provide transform-moment ingredients, but neither conditions graph-selected intervention inference on a matching validated global certificate with propagated precision bounds.
body.consumer: A certified prospective benchmark obtains uncertainty from replicate wells without manufacturing pseudo-single-cell observations.
body.proof_tex:
Apply the stratified PGF limit separately to the independent training and inference splits.  It gives
\[
\widehat g_A\overset p\longrightarrow g_0,\qquad
\widehat g_B\overset p\longrightarrow g_0,\qquad
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat g_B-g_0)
\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,\Sigma_g). \tag{30}
\]
Certification gives full rank, positive normalized row fractions, positive wrong-graph separation, global within-graph identification, a positive Jacobian margin, and positive clearance of every inference box.  The polynomial regularity lemma gives continuity on every compact graph box and continuous differentiability near the truth.

For any graph \(\boldsymbol d\), the minimized criterion is continuous in its data argument.  More explicitly, because every moment vector lies in the compact cube and \(W\) is fixed,
\[
\sup_{\vartheta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}
\left|Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta;\widehat g_A)
-Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta;g_0)\right|
\leq C\|\widehat g_A-g_0\|_2
+\|W\|_2\|\widehat g_A-g_0\|_2^2=o_p(1) \tag{31}
\]
for a finite deterministic \(C\), uniformly over the finite graph set.  The true graph has population minimum zero.  Every wrong graph has population minimum at least
\(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\).  Equation (31) and the fixed graph tie order therefore imply
\[
\Pr(\widehat{\boldsymbol D}=\boldsymbol D_0)\longrightarrow1. \tag{32}
\]

On the true graph, the certified global-identification lemma makes \(\theta_0\) the unique population minimum.  Compactness, (31) for the inference split, and the cited extremum-consistency theorem give
\(\widehat\theta\to_p\theta_0\) on the event in (32).  Positive inference-box clearance and the true-parameter interior assumption make the exact global minimizer interior with probability tending to one.  Put
\[
J_0=J_{\boldsymbol D_0,\mathcal T}(\theta_0).
\]
Certification gives \(\sigma_{\min}(J_0)>0\); with \(W\succ0\), \(J_0^{\mathsf T}WJ_0\) is invertible.  The cited minimum-distance theorem, with (30), yields
\[
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)
=(J_0^{\mathsf T}WJ_0)^{-1}J_0^{\mathsf T}W
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat g_B-g_0)+o_p(1), \tag{33}
\]
and the covariance in (33) is exactly
\(V_\theta(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0)\).

The training event in (32) is independent of the inference split.  For any bounded continuous test function, replacing the selected estimator by the true-graph estimator changes its expectation by at most twice the function bound times the probability of the complement of (32).  Thus the same limit holds unconditionally.  Differentiability of the fixed truncated-factorization contrast and a first-order Taylor expansion give
\[
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}-\boldsymbol\tau)
=C_\tau(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0;\iota)
\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat\theta-\theta_0)+o_p(1),
\]
whose covariance is the declared \(V_\tau\).

The empirical same-well products consistently estimate every \(\Omega_j\) by the stratified lemma.  Continuity of all matrix products and inverses on the certified nonsingular neighborhood, together with consistency of \(\widehat\theta\), proves plug-in consistency for \(\Sigma_g,V_\theta,V_\tau\).  The contrast-nondegeneracy assumption makes every reported scalar limiting variance strictly positive.  Slutsky's theorem then gives pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\) for each scalar Wald interval.  No uniform assertion at a graph or variance boundary is used.

Finally, the covariance factorization and spectral submultiplicativity give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma_g\|_2
&=\|D_gA_{\mathcal T}D_h^{-1}\Sigma_h
D_h^{-1}A_{\mathcal T}^{\mathsf T}D_g\|_2\\
&\leq\|D_g\|_2^2\|A_{\mathcal T}\|_2^2
\|D_h^{-1}\|_2^2\|\Sigma_h\|_2\\
&=\|\operatorname{diag}(g)\|_2^2\|M^+\|_2^2
\|\operatorname{diag}(h)^{-1}\|_2^2\|\Sigma_h\|_2,
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(\|M^+\otimes I_L\|_2=\|M^+\|_2\).  This is the stated pooling-amplification bound.
